paper_metadata.title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF STRUCTURE AND PHASE COMPOSITION FOR ALLOYS 45Kh26N33S2B2 AND 45X25H20C2 AFTER LONG-TERM EXPOSURE TO HIGH TEMPERATURES AND STATIC LOAD

evidence.quote: The high-temperature sections of radiative coils in pyrolysis systems used for ethylene production are fabricated from carbide-hardened heat-resistant austenitic alloys of base composition 45Kh25N35S2.

Comparative studies of the structural and phase composition of 45Kh25N20S2 steel (foreign-manufactured centrifugally cast pipe) and 45Kh26N33S2B2 (centrifugally cast pipe produced by Prometei) were performed both before and after a long-term strength test at 800–1100°C.

Comparative studies of the structural and phase composition of 45Kh25N20S2 steel (foreign-manufactured centrifugally cast pipe) and 45Kh26N33S2B2 (centrifugally cast pipe produced by Prometei) were performed both before and after a long-term strength test at 800–1100°C.

phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

attributes.location: alternating with chromium-rich carbide in carbide eutectic

evidence.quote: In 45Kh25N20S2 steel, the sections that were analyzed were found to consist of alternating sheets of austenite and chromium-rich (Table 1) carbide component 0.3–0.5 µm in width, identified as chromium carbide Cr7C3 (Table 2).

phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

evidence.quote: The intragranular precipitates are Cr23C6 carbides (see Table 2).

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr23C6
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: after long-term strength testing

attributes.morphology: massive particles fragmented; disperse; needle-shaped 3–5 µm or more in length
attributes.location: intercrystallite; boundary strips; interior of crystallites

evidence.quote: All the intercrystallite precipitates in the material under study were identified as Cr23C6 (see Table 2); it was also found that all the massive particles identified by optical and scanning electron metallography fragmented along large-angle boundaries in such a way that each particle is a set of smaller carbides (0.5–1 µm).

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr7C3
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

evidence.quote: Transmission electron microscopy studies indicate that the sheet eutectics consist of alternating layers of austenite and Cr7C3 (Table 3).

phases_and_microstructures.name: NbC
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

attributes.location: grain boundary; interior of columnar crystallites

evidence.quote: The niobium-rich intercrystallite precipitates have been identified as NbC carbides (see Table 3). x-Ray spectroscopic analysis indicates that both the Cr-containing and Nb-containing carbides are rich in (up to 1–3%) refractory elements such as Mo and W.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr23C6
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: as-cast

evidence.quote: The more massive particles, which are distributed along micrograin boundaries and have thicknesses of 0.1–0.5 µm and lengths of 0.2–1 µm, are identified as the carbide Cr23C6 (see Table 3).

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr23C6
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: after long-term strength testing at 800°C and 70 MPa for 5587 h

evidence.quote: Depending on the temperature and duration of the tests, precipitates of equiaxial (0.1–0.3 µm) or needle-shaped (5–10 µm in length) carbide particles (Cr23C6) were observed at 800°C in the boundary areas with higher etchability and at 900°C and 1000°C throughout the entire interior volume of the cells.

evidence.quote: Transmission electron microscope studies indicate that the massive-grain-boundary phases are complex features (conglomerates) with disperse internal structure, and consist of micronal and submicronal Cr23C6, Cr–Fe–Ni–Nb, Cr–Ni–Fe, Nb3Ni2Si5, NbC, Nb2C, Nb5Si, and Nb3Si particles (see Table 8 and Fig. 4) that give the mesh frame thermal stability, thereby improving the operational specifications for the resulting alloy.
